full_judgment: 4. Upon hearing the parties, the learned Assistant Judge dismissed the suit against which the plaintiff-respondent took an appeal and the appellate Court allowed the appeal and decreed the suit in part declaring plaintiff's title to the 2 'Ka' schedule land and also for recovery of his khash possession of the same directing the plaintiff to execute a deed of gift in respect of the land of schedule No.1 and also directing the defendant-college to prepare a donars list inserting the name of the plaintiff therein. Against the judgment of the appellate Court, the petitioner herein as defendant No.1 moved the High Court Division in revision and the High Court Division by the impugned judgment set aside the aforesaid appellate judgment and decree declaring title in both the schedules of the plaintiff and also allowing khash possession thereof. The petitioner filed civil petition for leave to appeal against the judgment of the High Court Division. Upon hearing the parties, this Division dismissed the leave-petition finding to the effect that the High Court Division in the exercise of revisional jurisdiction dismissed the suit on the ground of limitation whereas the appellate Court as a final Court of fact came to the finding that the suit was not barred by lamination. Upon consideration of materials on record this Division upheld the decision of the High Court Division.
